reviewer.method: One independent context applying four audience perspectives, not four independent experts. No delegation, author conversation, other threads or prior stage judgments were consulted.
reviewer.limits: Ordinal communication assessment of the supplemental overview. This is not a new deployment certification, a statistical comparison, or an assessment of all 126 source PDF pages. No Azure resources were provisioned, no artifacts repaired and nothing published.

scope: Final single integrated solution/platform visual, judged against overview-brief.md, rubric.json, the supplied composition reference, and relevant frozen Stage 5 model and narrative evidence.
summary: The overview is a readable, genuinely integrated poster with strong isolation and recovery caveats. All 56 canonical component IDs and all 97 active flow records are preserved. However, the primary proposal bridge is placed in the wrong regional plane, and the combined US partner/identity label drops the source's non-regional identity qualification. These are material overview defects, not inherited deployment limitations. Smaller problems concern incomplete narrative-only regional mapping, the equipment subscription boundary, first-time-reader navigation and visibility of security exceptions.

findings.title: Primary proposal bridge is drawn in the wrong regional plane

evidence.location: bridge card x2430 y2080 w520 h200, inside CENTRAL US customer-dedicated equipment plane; A25 enters from Cosmos and A26 crosses to primary API
Page 1, lower-center equipment panel and upper-right drapps card
Line 488: bridge is East US 2 P1v3 with integration 10.40.11.0/24 and local API/agent private endpoints; lines 576-581: premium adds a counterpart in the separate Central US business network
Page 37 bridge row; page 44 premium API/sync/bridge row

findings.explanation: Stage 5 puts the normal bridge beside the business API, reading Cosmos across regions. The overview instead puts its canonical bridge in Central US equipment and draws the API request across regions. The drapps card also lists a regional bridge counterpart. This reverses which normal dependency is cross-region and obscures which business network owns the bridge's private access and recovery. The source narrative is explicit; this is not an inherited unresolved placement.
findings.requestedRevision: Represent the canonical bridge in East US 2 business services and retain its premium counterpart in the separate Central US business region, or use an explicitly location-neutral logical grouping that states both placements. Update A25/A26 and the sidecar consistently. No change to the frozen design is needed.

findings.title: Combined US partner/identity label loses a material residency qualification

evidence.location: partners card x80 y1320 w480 h180: US partner / identity endpoints, containing Entra / Graph / approved build endpoints
Page 1, left external-endpoint card reached by A13
Line 680 explicitly excludes global Azure identity, control-plane and DNS metadata from US-exclusive claims
Page 53, first paragraph under Security and data

findings.explanation: The US modifier visually applies to the combined group, not only the CRM. Neither the card nor the poster legend restores the source's distinction between US business content and non-regional identity/control metadata. This can lead a residency review to accept a stronger claim than the source makes. It is a misleading overview label, not evidence of an actual data-residency violation.
findings.requestedRevision: Separate the US CRM qualification from global or tenant-dependent identity/control endpoints and explicitly preserve the metadata exception on the visual.

primarySource.quote: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) operates as a non-regional service and based on customer requirements, including availability and scalability, may store Microsoft Entra directory data globally.
primarySource.qualification: This does not mean every tenant's directory data is stored globally. It establishes that a blanket US-only inference from the diagram is unsupported. Tenant-specific residency needs its own evidence.

findings.title: Physical equipment sits inside the Azure production-subscription outline

evidence.location: premium-subscription bounds x650 y610 w3690 h2080 contain equipment card x710 y2080 w480 h200
Legend says devices are outside the Central US region, but does not explain their placement inside the production subscription
equipment and equipment-ops nodes: customer equipment and customer-owned commissioning/maintenance

findings.explanation: The devices are correctly outside the Azure equipment-region rectangle and explicitly labeled customer US sites. However, unlike the mobile client and on-prem ERP, they remain inside an outline labeled production subscription. That weakens the ownership grammar. The label mitigates the ambiguity, so this is not treated as a deployment blocker.
findings.requestedRevision: Keep the physical-device card outside the subscription outline, or label the enclosing shape as a logical customer solution boundary and draw Azure subscription ownership separately.

findings.title: Canonical-ID coverage is stronger than narrative-only regional coverage

evidence.location: Components table: drapps maps api-dr/executor-dr; drstores maps vault-dr/evidence-dr; introductory statement groups unnamed regional counterparts
drapps and drstores cards in Central US warm business region omit explicit regional ingestion/agent, quarantine/scanner and immutable audit-copy responsibilities
Page 44 Ingestion and agent apps; page 45 Quarantine/scanning and Audit and holds

findings.explanation: The source adds meaningful regional dependencies without creating canonical -dr IDs for every one. The overview's broad grouping disclaimer does not map these rows to an explicit group or omission record. All 56 IDs being present is therefore insufficient to prove every material narrative subsystem is accounted for. Primary versions remain visible, and no automatic all-store recovery is claimed, which limits the severity.
findings.requestedRevision: Add exact source-row-to-group mappings for narrative-only regional dependencies and distinguish shown, summarized and intentionally omitted detail. Separate new diagrams are unnecessary.

Numbered overview journeys, particularly A7: direct API/sync SQL paths intentionally not drawn

findings.explanation: The sidecar explains the numbers, and the SQL card identifies durable responsibilities. This prevents a coverage failure, but a junior reader can mistake the visually prominent API-to-worker-to-SQL chain for a mandatory AI path. The poster also starts numbering with release management rather than a complete customer journey. This limits immediate teaching value without making the artifact unreadable.
findings.requestedRevision: Supply a compact human-journey reading guide and expand the most important terms. Make direct case-state ownership or the intentional omission unmistakable.

findings.title: Important security exceptions survive mainly in the detailed source

evidence.location: objects, iot, processing, cosmos and recovery-gates text; scanner pending/error and public device ingress are visible, but scanner network exception and ServiceConnect residual scope are not
Page 29 scanner resource-instance exception; page 37 ServiceConnect broader-than-consumer-group scope
Lines 520 and 674: bridge container-write residual privilege and security sign-off gates
original_flows 61/68/70 and coverage identity-access/security retain relevant source details

findings.explanation: The poster does not falsely claim that private endpoints alone disable public access. Nevertheless, its unresolved-gates summary emphasizes availability and capacity while security reviewers must search elsewhere for the exceptional scanner route, broad hub credential and bridge write privilege. These are inherited source risks whose prominence is reduced by the overview, not new vulnerabilities introduced by a diagram.
findings.requestedRevision: Give the three residual permissions or network exceptions a short visible callout and exact source references. Do not imply that the diagram resolves or approves them.

subsystemMappingAudit.subsystem: Provider ownership, governance and release control
subsystemMappingAudit.note: A1/A2/A27/A28 distinguish releases and allowlisted metadata from runtime. Nonproduction is explicitly additional and synthetic. Provider subscription regional details are summarized rather than fully drawn.
40 dedicated premium and 160 standard customers are explicit, without a cross-customer data route. O1 and O3 qualify regional and subscription-boundary correctness.

Grouped actors and SSO are distinct from provider ownership. Issuer/session/ACL enforcement and source lifecycle details remain in the detailed pack; A3 is a client request, not an identity-provider payload proxy.

subsystemMappingAudit.note: Managed app/data services remain outside primary VNet; private NICs and outbound integration are distinguished. Firewall and VPN are grouped, not a claim that they share a required deployment subnet. Individual data PE/DNS paths are explicitly omitted.

subsystemMappingAudit.subsystem: Case, mobile and workflow authoritative state
subsystemMappingAudit.note: Separate identities/plans, deterministic authorization, exact versions/expiry and regional epoch are visible. API SQL links and approval state transitions are not separately drawn; see O5.
Source ACL/deletion, untrusted documents, US Data Zone and no agent execution credentials are visible. Regional narrative-only replicas need O4's mapping.
Separate accounts and pending/error never clean are explicit; scanner-specific access and regional replicas need clearer references (O4/O6).
Local secrets, support audit and content-free fleet export are clear. This is not proof of executed audit/retention tests; regional immutable copies are not individually mapped.
Eight-hour grant, assigned subset, local encryption, server rechecks and noninstant wipe are visible. A30 reaches the same WAF as normal case ingress.

Private ERP, public CRM, uncertain effects and customer-isolated overlapping addresses are retained. O2 concerns the identity endpoint geography label, not ERP placement. Retired flow 41 is not restored.

Device certificates, signed maintenance, public ingress, per-customer fixture scale and separate telemetry network are visible. Physical subscription placement is ambiguous (O3); credential exception prominence is limited (O6).

requirementChecks.criterion: Readability as one integrated visual, including dense regions, crossings, labels, contrast and zoom/print usability
evidence: overview/solution-platform-overview.svg: full canvas and readable-scale browser views
overview/solution-platform-overview.pdf:1 full page and six overlapping crops
requirementChecks.assessment: This is one integrated architecture, not a contact sheet. Typography and icons remain readable at appropriate zoom; dense A12/A13, A18-A20/A28, A25/A26 and A29 regions have traceable routes without observed text collisions. Crossings are explicitly not joins. The reference's nested boundaries, external managed services and orthogonal numbered connectors are adapted without copying its product lineup or branding. A 1.2-meter poster cannot be read as a normal chat thumbnail or A3 handout, and that trade-off is honestly documented.

requirementChecks.criterion: Usefulness for junior developer, CTO, enterprise architect and security architect
requirementChecks.assessment: Useful for executive orientation and guided developer/security discussion. It is not yet reliable for independent enterprise-architecture placement review because of O1/O2. O5 limits immediate teaching value. One persona has scores below 3, so the rubric's pass threshold is not met.

inheritedSourceLimitations.limitation: Premium availability/recovery targets are unproved; asynchronous SQL loss and old external effects are not solved by DNS or an epoch.
inheritedSourceLimitations.overviewTreatment: Accurately prominent in drsql, drstores and recovery gates. Not a new overview defect and not penalized merely because Azure drills were out of scope.

inheritedSourceLimitations.limitation: Scanner network exception, ServiceConnect residual scope and bridge write privileges need security acceptance.
inheritedSourceLimitations.overviewTreatment: Preserved in detailed mapping/source but less visible on the poster; O6 concerns communication, not a claim that the reviewer discovered an implemented exploit.

inheritedSourceLimitations.limitation: Capacity, regional model support/quota, evidence availability, commercial nonproduction count and recovery staffing remain unconfirmed.
inheritedSourceLimitations.overviewTreatment: Mostly disclosed. No price, quota, deployability or measured service commitment was inferred from SKU labels.

decisionRule: Revise because O1 and O2 are major overview defects, five assessment criteria are partial, and enterprise-architect scores fall below 3. Artifact inspection was possible, so blocked is not appropriate. The readable poster and passing integrity checker cannot cancel these findings. A future passing overview would still not overturn a failed source-stage deployment-realism judgment.
